title: Constrained stream rewrite validator for legacy SDK compatibility
creator: Ava Kim
description: Goal: build an automated validation harness that exercises constrained-decoding enforcement on streaming responses while simultaneously applying a rewrite/compatibility layer (SDK shim) that maps new structured JSON outputs back to legacy SDK shapes. The validator should simulate partial emits, token truncation, interleaved tool calls, and KV cache reuse to verify both strict schema adherence and pragmatic brittle-to-resilient rewrites used by older clients. This ticket covers design, implementation of the harness, test cases, and integration with canary runs in the console testplane.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 3 predefined scenarios (full-schema, partial-emit, interleaved-toolcall) against a stubbed model and record pass/fail
Compatibility layer converts at least 95% of valid new-schema outputs to legacy SDK shapes without data loss for canonical test prompts
Failure modes are annotated with deterministic repair hints (repair token insertions or structural mapping suggestions) in the test logs
Canary integration: harness can be executed as part of the 'schema-gate-canary' job and produce a dashboardable pass rate metric
Automated regression tests added in CI that fail when constrained-decoder enforcement is bypassed in streaming mode
test_plan: Scenario A: Strict stream with complete JSON payload - verify pass and no rewrites
Scenario B: Partial-token truncation mid-object - verify constrained decoder attempts graceful recovery and logs repair suggestions
Scenario C: Interleaved toolcall tokens inserted - validate detection and recovery path, check shim mapping preserves tool outputs
Scenario D: Legacy-shape mapping - feed new-schema responses and assert SDK shim output matches legacy contract for 100 sample prompts
Chaos run: inject 5-10% token drop across stream windows and measure pass / graceful-degrade behavior
implementation_notes: Reuse existing stream test framework from ENG-14266 for token-level simulation
Implement a compact compatibility map (compat-map) that is rule-first: key renames, flattening, and optional field fallback rules
Provide a synthetic model stub that emits configurable patterns (complete, truncated, toolcall-interleaved) to keep tests deterministic
Collect structured logs in NDJSON with fields: scenario, seed, decoded_schema, shim_actions, recovery_steps
Expose metric 'schema_compat_pass_rate' to Console for canary visualization
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created and scoped. Spike planned to evaluate current harness gaps.
2025-02-12: Spike complete - identified missing token-drop simulation and legacy-shim harness. Decided to implement compat-map DSL (rule-based) rather than ML mapper to keep deterministic behavior.
2025-02-14: Prototype of synthetic stub and basic compat-map done. End-to-end local run for Scenario A passes.
2025-02-17: Added partial-emit recovery heuristics + logging. Began writing CI job definition and dashboard metric plumbing.
2025-02-18: First review with PM and DX. Received design feedback (see review_feedback).
review_feedback: PM (Rohit Gupta): Good scope; emphasize measurable thresholds for legacy mapping to avoid silent data loss
Design (Lena Zhou): Add a sample mapping UI prototype for Console so customers can preview shim behavior before enabling
Security (Maya Patel): Confirm that compat-map rules do not leak internal PII transformations. Suggested review checklist added
Eng (Samir Naidu): Recommend starting with synchronous CI runs; streaming canary will be gated after first green
risks: Over-eager rewrites could hide real schema regressions from downstream customers
Deterministic rule-based mapping may not cover complex nested transforms required by some legacy clients
Performance impact in streaming path if compat-map is applied synchronously to every partial emit
qa_results: Local runs: Scenario A pass (100/100), Scenario B partial recovery recorded (83/100 pass with repair hints)
Early CI: smoke job created but gated until canary metrics are visible in staging
Manual review: Sample shimbed outputs inspected and signed off by PM for 25 canonical prompts
next_steps: Complete compat-map DSL and publish example rule library
Add Console preview component (design handoff to DX) and link toggle in canary UI
Wire 'schema_compat_pass_rate' metric to canary dashboard and schedule a 24-hour run in staging
Follow-up security review to confirm transform ruleset cannot be abused for PII exfiltration
After green canary, extend CI gating to include streaming regression tests for all supported models
